Subject: ACME - Post-demo model shortlist & next steps

Thanks again for taking the time to demo with us earlier today — really appreciated the thoughtful questions from you and Pat. Per our conversation, I wanted to summarize the recommended shortlist of model options and the tradeoffs (cost / latency / quality) we discussed, plus next steps for evaluation.

Quick recap of ACME's priorities (from discovery):
- High throughput for search re-ranking and summary generation (peak 600 qps)
- Tight latency requirements for interactive UIs (~150ms P95)
- Strong quality on instruction-following and factuality for customer-facing outputs
- Enterprise requirements: SOC 2 evidence + SSO, and private deployment is a possible requirement later this year

Recommended shortlist (rationale + tradeoffs):
1) Llama-3-70B (quantized FP16) — Recommended as primary for quality-sensitive tasks
   - Quality: highest on instruction and summarization benchmarks in our eval set
   - Latency: higher baseline but acceptable when served on dedicated A100s with optimized kernels
   - Cost: mid-to-high; recommended for critical paths where quality matters

2) OpenMPT-30B (int8) — Strong cost/latency balance for large-scale re-ranking
   - Quality: solid for ranking / paraphrase tasks, slightly weaker on long-form summarization
   - Latency: noticeably better throughput and lower cost per token when batched
   - Cost: low-to-mid; good candidate for default route with fallback to 70B for edge cases

3) RedTiny-8B (distilled, fp16) — Cost-efficient for low-latency interactive flows
   - Quality: good for short prompts and UI-level suggestions, not recommended for final-customer summaries
   - Latency: excellent; meets 150ms P95 on dedicated inference instances
   - Cost: low; ideal for high-volume completion paths

Attached: high-level benchmark report, prompt set used in eval, and an initial cost estimate spreadsheet.
[attachment: benchmark_report.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)]
[attachment: prompt_set_v1.csv (CSV, 12KB)]
[attachment: model_cost_estimates.xlsx (XLSX, 85KB)]

Proposed evaluation plan / next steps:
- We can run a 2-week A/B evaluation using your test prompts (included) across the three candidates. Redwood will provide the eval harness, capture token-level costs, and quality metrics (ROUGE/BLANC-like proxies, human spot checks).
- Deliverables: dataset of outputs, latency/cost dashboard, recommended production routing policy (e.g., default -> OpenMPT-30B, fallback -> Llama-3-70B for low-confidence cases).
- Exec decision needed: approval to run the A/B on the dedicated sandbox environment and confirmation of POC license (we estimate ~3-4k USD for the 2-week run for dedicated infra).

Can we schedule a 30-min follow-up to lock the test prompts and timing? I'm available Tue/Wed mornings PT.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: ACME - Post-demo model shortlist & next steps

Thanks Jamie — great questions. Short answers below and attached the appendix with representative regression cases.

1) Expected latency (measured on our dedicated A100 80GB profile, 1k warmup tokens, batch sizes tuned):
   - Llama-3-70B (quantized FP16): P50 ~120ms, P95 ~240ms (single-request baseline). With batching and kernel optimizations targeting re-ranking, P95 can be reduced ~15-25% depending on request distribution.
   - OpenMPT-30B (int8): P50 ~60ms, P95 ~110ms. Designed for high-throughput routing.
   - RedTiny-8B (fp16 distilled): P50 ~20-35ms, P95 ~60-90ms.

2) Low-confidence/fallback logic:
   - We support several configurable signals: log-prob thresholds, ensemble disagreement, and retrieval-based grounding confidence. You can choose which signals and set thresholds via the Redwood Console routing rules. We typically recommend a combined score (ensemble + LM log-prob) for production fallbacks.

3) Cost breakdown (high level; details in attached XLSX):
   - Infra (dedicated GPU hours): ~55% of POC estimate
   - Token compute (per-token cost based on model profile): ~35%
   - Platform and tooling (monitoring, eval harness): ~10%

Attachments: short_regressions_appendix.txt (excerpt), updated model_cost_estimates.xlsx.
[attachment: short_regressions_appendix.txt (TXT, 8KB)]

Looping in Vivek and Neha to confirm the sandbox sizing and SOC 2 evidence questions.

Best,
Marissa

Internal note — quick checklist before the Tue call: 
- Confirm we can produce the 70B P95 numbers on A100 80GB for their traffic (need 2x instance warmup and kernel tuning). I'll schedule a short perf run.
- Prepare the regression appendix: include 4 cases (2 hallucinations, 2 attribution errors) with model outputs and prompt context. Marissa: the external appendix you attached is good; expand one more hallucination example.
- SOC 2 / evidence: have the standard packet ready (SOC2 report link, system architecture diagram). Neha: can you attach the SOC2 pack to the HubSpot deal after the call?
